policy: Every approval below is a second-pass verification of the correction already recorded by the row-by-row audit. No independent build-time correction is introduced.

approvals.approval_note: Second-pass verified spelling: plaît requires the circumflex; meaning is otherwise unchanged.

approvals.approved_target: Qu'est-ce que tu as mangé aujourd'hui ?

audit_basis.recommended: Qu'est-ce que tu as mangé aujourd'hui ? / What did you eat today?

approvals.approval_note: Second-pass verified: passé composé mangé correctly matches the English simple-past eating event.

approvals.approved_target: Qu'est-ce que tu voulais que je fasse ?
approvals.approved_english: What did you want me to do?

audit_basis.recommended: Qu'est-ce que tu voulais que je fasse ? / What did you want me to do?

approvals.approval_note: Second-pass verified: the French past vouloir is correctly represented by English past 'did you want', not the original conditional-style gloss.

approvals.approved_target: Pourquoi as-tu besoin de mon aide ?
approvals.approved_english: Why do you need my help?

audit_basis.recommended: Pourquoi as-tu besoin de mon aide ? / Why do you need my help?

approvals.approval_note: Second-pass verified: avoir besoin de means need; the corrected English restores lexical equivalence.

approvals.approved_english: Do you know where they are?
approvals.approval_note: Second-pass verified subject-verb agreement: plural ils requires sont.

approvals.approved_target: Qu'est-ce que tu as acheté pour ton petit ami ?
approvals.approved_english: What did you buy your boyfriend?

audit_basis.recommended: Qu'est-ce que tu as acheté pour ton petit ami ?

approvals.approval_note: Second-pass verified orthography: standard interrogative form is Qu'est-ce que.

audit_basis.recommended: Que faisais-tu là-bas ? / What were you doing there?

approvals.approval_note: Second-pass verified: the French imparfait denotes ongoing/background activity and is accurately matched by English past progressive.
